U.S. Embassy Consular Update: Cancelation of Visa Interview Appointments on November 17
https://t.co/tMKHAmMzWT

The U.S. Embassy in the Philippines will be closed for visa appointments on Monday, November 17 due to the expected heavy traffic and road closures near the embassy, related to scheduled rallies from November 16 to 18.

For affected nonimmigrant visa applicants, please reschedule your November 17 appointment through our online appointment system by logging in to your account at https://t.co/QH9rQ23hbW. The Embassy opened additional nonimmigrant visa interview slots to provide applicants with schedule options.

Immigrant visa applicants will receive detailed instructions through their registered email address regarding their new appointment or rescheduling options.

The U.S. Embassy is not canceling appointments for Tuesday, November 18, but please monitor our social media and your email for any updates or changes.

The offsite Visa Application Center (VAC) in Parañaque City will remain open on November 17 for all scheduled biometrics (photo and fingerprint collection) appointments.

For updates on visa operations, please visit our website at https://t.co/DXhUdBrJv9.

MENDIOLA HINARANGAN NA NG BARBED-WIRE

Barbed-wire fences were installed by the Manila Police District near the Mendiola Peace Arch on Friday, November 14, 2025, in preparation for the upcoming protest on November 30.

The Philippine National Police warned demonstrators that security protocols would be stricter and that any acts of violence would not be tolerated, as authorities brace for a potential large-scale anti-corruption rally following President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s call for a peaceful demonstration ahead of the “Trillion Peso March” sequel. | via Jonas Sulit, Abante
